description: Who each program is for, how to adjust it, and what volume it delivers.

tags.Well supported: Consistent findings across reviews or a position stand.
tags.Moderate: Supported, but limited by study size, population or design.
tags.Standard practice: Widely used convention without strong direct evidence.
tags.Contested: Published evidence disagrees or is thin; Gideon should say so.
tags.Library design: A deliberate choice in how these plans are built.
tags.Definition: Plain-language meaning of a term used in the app.

common.daysPerWeek: 3 core training days, plus an optional 4th training day (template day 6). Two recovery days and one rest day.
common.sessionLength: Training days 45 minutes or less including warm-up and cool-down. Recovery days 30 minutes or less.
common.equipment: Every program works in all four setups: Full Gym, Home Gym (Barbell + Dumbbells), Dumbbells Only, Bodyweight Only.
common.structure: 52 weeks in 13 four-week blocks. Week 4 of each block is a lighter deload week.

equipmentNote: Engine, Pulse, Warrior and Valkyrie rely on conditioning and power movements that work in every setup but feel best with a bit of space.

programs.bestFor: Getting stronger on the big lifts with a simple full-body structure.
programs.notIdeal: Chasing maximum muscle size or athletic power.
programs.pairing: Add Built for a size block after a strength base. Hard conditioning on top can blunt lower-body strength, mainly in men.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Forged is a strength plan. Volume is moderate, and chest, hamstrings and calves are light compared with a size plan.

programs.bestFor: Building muscle with higher-rep full-body work and an arm finisher.
programs.pairing: Follow a Forged block, or alternate blocks with Forged. See the volume audit: chest and hamstrings are light.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Built is the size plan, but chest, glutes, hamstrings and calves fall below 10 weekly sets even on the 4-day version, while shoulders run high. Describe this honestly if asked.

programs.bestFor: Fitness, work capacity and a harder cardio challenge.
programs.notIdeal: Maximal strength or size goals. It has no arm finisher.
programs.pairing: Best run as its own plan or in a separate block from heavy leg training.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Engine is built from timed circuits, not set-and-rep lifting, so weekly sets per muscle do not apply.

programs.bestFor: Power, speed and grit through fast lifts, circuits and combat conditioning.
programs.notIdeal: Brand-new lifters. Volume is low by design.
programs.pairing: Build a strength base with Forged first if you are new to lifting.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Warrior is a low-volume strength and power plan by design. All muscle groups are under 10 weekly sets.

programs.bestFor: Getting stronger on the big lifts, with bone-loading work on the optional day.
programs.notIdeal: Chasing maximum muscle size or athletic power.
programs.pairing: Add Sculpted for a shape-and-size block after a strength base.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Rooted is a strength plan with glute emphasis. Hamstrings and chest are light.

programs.bestFor: Building muscle with a glute, leg and shoulder emphasis and an arm finisher.
programs.pairing: Follow a Rooted block, or alternate blocks with Rooted. See the volume audit: chest and hamstrings are light.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Sculpted is the size and shape plan. Glutes are well covered, but chest and hamstrings are on the light side and calves are minimal.

programs.bestFor: Fitness, work capacity and a harder cardio challenge.
programs.notIdeal: Maximal strength or size goals. It has no arm finisher.
programs.pairing: Best run as its own plan or in a separate block from heavy leg training.
programs.howToDescribeVolume: Pulse is built from timed circuits, not set-and-rep lifting, so weekly sets per muscle do not apply.

programs.notIdeal: Brand-new lifters. Volume is low by design.

adjustmentRecipes.answer: Run the 3 core training days and skip the optional 4th day.
adjustmentRecipes.mechanism: Template day 6 is optional and only shown when the 4th training day is turned on.

adjustmentRecipes.answer: Keep the main lifts first and drop accessories from the bottom of the list. Skip the arm finisher before skipping a main lift.
adjustmentRecipes.mechanism: Exercise order is priority order; the arm finisher is last.

adjustmentRecipes.answer: Repeat the last week you finished rather than jumping ahead. Do not try to make up every missed session.
adjustmentRecipes.mechanism: Advice only. Confirm how the app advances plan days before promising a specific behavior.

adjustmentRecipes.situation: Back after 3 or more weeks off
adjustmentRecipes.answer: Restart near the previous lighter-week load and build back over about two weeks. Keep 3 or more reps in reserve at first.

adjustmentRecipes.situation: Stalled for 3 or more weeks on a lift
adjustmentRecipes.answer: Hold the weight, check form and general habits (sleep, stress, consistency), and take the lighter week early if you feel run down. Do not diagnose or prescribe food.
Switch to the Dumbbells Only or Bodyweight Only setup. The session stays the same and the movements swap to a version that fits.
adjustmentRecipes.mechanism: byEquipment on every movement in movements.json.

adjustmentRecipes.answer: Move to Built (men) or Sculpted (women) at the start of the next 4-week block. Note that chest and hamstring volume is on the lighter side in the current plans.
adjustmentRecipes.mechanism: Plan switch at a block boundary.

adjustmentRecipes.answer: Swap the optional 4th day for an Engine-style or Pulse-style day, or run a conditioning block. Keep hard intervals off heavy leg days.
Use the app's alternate, or step down the Progressions ladder to an easier version. Quality first, then add load or difficulty.
Mild soreness is normal. Train at lower effort (leave 3 or more reps in reserve), shorten the session, or move to an easy walk. Pain is different: see the Boundaries tab.
Start with Forged or Rooted, learn each movement with light loads, use the easier versions from Progressions and aim for consistency before intensity.
Run the Intake and Screening steps first. Then build only from the generator rules: allowed session types, movement swaps by pattern, volume ceilings, and the required warm-up and cool-down.

volumeAudit.method: Method: counts set-and-rep work only. The first-listed muscle on each movement counts as 1 set per set; other listed muscles count as 0.5. Core holds, carries, timed circuits and warm-ups are excluded. Averaged over the 39 non-deload weeks of the 52-week plan. Muscle tags in movements.json are coarse, so treat this as a screening tool, not a prescription. Reference points: ACSM's review suggests about 10 or more sets per muscle per week for size and 2 to 3 sets per lift for strength.
volumeAudit.decision: Decision (2026-11-08): leave plan volume as is for now. Revisit chest, hamstrings and calves in Built, Sculpted, Forged and Rooted later.
